name: Three
summary: Three recurs as a marker of a completed span -- most often three days -- at several of Scripture's pivotal moments, and underlies the Christian doctrine of the Trinity.

claims.text: Jonah is described as being in the belly of the great fish three days and three nights.
Jesus explicitly compares his own coming death and resurrection to Jonah's three days and three nights.
The Gospels place Jesus' resurrection on the third day after his crucifixion.

Threefold repetition appears at other climactic moments, such as the seraphim's threefold 'Holy, holy, holy' describing God -- a literary device used elsewhere in Scripture to mark something as complete or emphatic.

Three is foundational to the Christian doctrine of the Trinity -- one God eternally existing as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. This is a theological formulation developed from the whole of Scripture and later church teaching, not a word count or a single verse's claim.

sources: Christianity.com, 'What Is the Significance of the Number 3 in the Bible?'
christianwebsite.com, 'Why Are Things Repeated Three Times In The Bible?'
